name: Erst
reason: Natural wine and communal tables both on, and the kitchen runs to 11pm.

name: Schofield's
reason: An award-winning cocktail list, with mixology done tableside.

name: Mana
reason: Michelin-recognised, with a chef's table if you want to watch the pass.

name: 20 Stories
reason: A skyline view and heated outdoor seating that actually gets used through a Manchester winter.

name: The Jane Eyre
reason: Booth seating and no music you have to shout over.

name: Blinker
reason: No sign on Tib Street. You have to already know it's there.

name: Matt & Phreds
reason: Live jazz until 1am in a room small enough to hear the brushes on the snare. No cover before nine.

name: The Ivy Spinningfields
reason: Formal service, a dress code, and sittings that run as late as 10.30pm.

name: Refuge
reason: A live pianist Thursday to Saturday, and a bar that keeps pouring well past midnight.

name: Tattu
reason: Set menus with a dessert course that comes with its own theatrics. Loudest room in the district after nine.

name: Victors
reason: Communal tables and a buzz built for groups. Worth the drive out on a Friday.

name: Pollen Bakery
reason: Canalside counter seats and viennoiserie out of the oven at eight.

name: Mackie Mayor
reason: Nine kitchens under one roof. Turn up with no plan and you'll still eat well.

name: Foundation Coffee
reason: A mill floor big enough to get actual work done in, with coffee good enough to justify a second.

name: The Wizard
reason: Fires lit from October, and the Edge walk finishes at the door.

name: The Old Cellars
reason: Sommelier on site and small plates until close.

name: Everyman Cinema
reason: Sofa seats in screen two. Order the wine before the trailers — they bring it to you.

name: Rudy's
reason: No bookings, but the queue after the late screening is usually nothing.

name: Porta
reason: One last sherry standing at the counter. Kitchen closes at midnight.

name: Happy Seasons
reason: Forty-odd years on Faulkner Street. The queue for the roast duck still forms before the doors open.

name: The Bull's Head
reason: Named best pub in Cheshire, then best in the whole North West. Mill Lane still has more sheep on it than sat-nav coverage.

name: HOME
reason: Five screens, two stages, and a gallery floor that changes over faster than you'd expect.

name: Band on the Wall
reason: A stage bolted high on the far wall since the thirties, reborn after a £3.5m rebuild. The touring act you half-recognise on the bill usually turns out to be the whole point of the night.

name: Manchester Art Gallery
reason: Free to walk in off Mosley Street and stand in front of the Pre-Raphaelites. The current dress-and-textile show, WORN, is worth the extra half hour.

name: Royal Exchange Theatre
reason: A glass module dropped into a Victorian trading hall. The largest theatre-in-the-round in the world, and close enough to hear the actors breathe.

name: The Wine Cellar
reason: Forty wines by the glass, and a slate of Courtyard Dairy cheese, on a Hawthorn Lane side street. Easy to mean to leave after one and not.

name: Altrincham Market
reason: Ten independent kitchens and two bars under one roof, open till ten most nights. Show up hungry and undecided — you won't stay either for long.

name: The Stolen Lamb
reason: Chef-owned Greek on Water Lane, more island cooking than taverna cliché. Regulars order the lamb chops and stop reading the rest of the menu.

name: Suburban Green
reason: Sister site to the Chorlton original, four doors down Hawthorn Lane from its own sibling Wine Cellar. Small plates built to share, and a wine list that turns over weekly.

name: Smoke Wilmslow
reason: Four generations of curing and smoking behind the bar snacks. Water Lane's café by day, cocktail room by night — same kitchen either way.

name: Symposium
reason: Grove Street's newest late licence. Upstairs booths built for the hour after everywhere else has called last orders.

name: Cibo
reason: Family-run on Green Lane. A retractable roof over the terrace, and a hundred and sixty covers that still feel like a neighbourhood table.

name: Cibo Gran Cafe
reason: The grander sibling to Cibo's Green Lane original, two minutes away in the Grove Arcade — a marble patisserie counter out front, a proper bar behind it, and a Sunday afternoon tea that runs to arancini and a tiered stand of tiramisu and mini cheesecake rather than just scones.

name: Piccolino Grande
reason: A £2m rebuild made this the most ambitious Piccolino outside London — marble, brass and a copper-clad pizza oven behind a winterised Tuscan terrace that runs straight through winter. The carbonara is finished tableside in a hollowed parmesan wheel, and the T-bone is proper Fassona Piedmontese rather than a supplier's default cut.

name: Heddy's
reason: A Water Lane institution, now with a second room in Alderley Edge. The mezze usually arrives before you've finished deciding what else to order.

name: Caramello
reason: Didsbury's original brunch room found a second home on Water Lane. Scratch-made plates, and a queue that starts before ten.

name: Wilmslow Tavern
reason: Simon and Kay's village-centre local out toward Dean Row. Proper pizza, a beer garden, and no pressure to give up the table.

name: Phanthong Thai
reason: Mum-and-daughter run on Alderley Road, next door to the King's Arms. The menu reads long, but it's hard to order badly off it.

name: Vietbowl
reason: Family-run home-style cooking on Bank Square. The kind of pho worth eating slowly.

name: Rex Cinema
reason: Art deco since 1936, dark for two decades, reborn in 2019. Plush seats, a proper bar, and the original REX signage still over the door.

name: The Carrs
reason: Seventy-one acres along the Bollin, gifted to the town by a Boddington. Named for the Norse word for bog-meadow, and still the walk that clears a working week.

name: Wilmslow Kitchen
reason: Sarah and David Bridge's cookery school on the Deanway estate, tucked behind a row of Ferrari and Porsche showrooms. Evening classes end with everyone sitting down to eat what they made.

name: Ricardo Van Parmar Gallery
reason: Private viewings by appointment on Alderley Road. Stock runs from emerging names to originals by Banksy and Warhol.

name: Wilmslow Artisan Market
reason: Grove Street and Bank Square close to traffic once a month for a hundred stalls of food, craft and live music. Check the date before building an evening around it.

name: Wilmslow RUFC
reason: Memorial Ground on Kings Road, a co-operatively owned club between the Carrs and the river. North West 1 rugby, then a proper clubhouse pint after.

name: Green Room Theatre
reason: A Victorian cottage and an old shirt factory, converted by the town's own amateur society. Founded 1924, one of the oldest in the country, and still selling out its hundred-and-two-seat house.

name: Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness
reason: Above a bakery on Hawthorn Lane, the same studio Tracey has taught from for over twenty years — small classes, monthly sound ceremonies, no scale in sight.

name: Wilmslow History Tours
reason: Free, two hours, departs the library at eleven. The Historical Society's own guide walks you into St Bartholomew's, on a site with a church since 1246.

name: Alchemy Personal Training
reason: A private studio off Hawthorn Walk, wet room and changing rooms included. One-to-one sessions, not a class timetable to fit yourself around.

name: Wilmslow Golf Club
reason: Great Warford's eighteen holes since the 1880s, shaped in turn by James Braid and Frederick Hawtree. Open qualifying history, on a course most of Cheshire only plays as a guest.

name: The Elk of Hale
reason: Family-run since 2013 on Ashley Road. An Alpine-lodge fit-out that shouldn't work in Cheshire and somehow does, with a spirits list that runs deeper than the room suggests.

name: Church Inn
reason: Opposite the twelfth-century church it's named for, and named best pub in the country more than once since. Book the snug or don't bother.

name: Aldeli
reason: A former car showroom turned New York deli on London Road. Salt beef bagels before noon, pancakes after.

name: Hallé St Peter's
reason: A deconsecrated Grade II church on Blossom Street, still the Hallé's own rehearsal hall. Public concerts happen in a room built for hymn acoustics, not a sound engineer.

name: BAB NQ
reason: Flatbreads made from scratch in an open kitchen. The basement cocktail room only opens once the sun's down.

name: Smolensky Gallery
reason: Polished concrete and street-art pedigree inside the ABC Building on Quay Street. Worth going before dinner, not tacking on after.

name: Podium Restaurant
reason: Two AA Rosettes some forty floors below Cloud 23. The kitchen holds its own against the view.

name: Hale Country Club & Spa
reason: Five thermal rooms and an infinity pool over its own stretch of Cheshire countryside. A members' club that still sells day passes.

name: Barnshaw Smithy
reason: Poached eggs and proper coffee next to a working reclamation yard, on the lane between Mobberley and Ashley that the sat-nav still hesitates over.

name: Nam
reason: Manchester's only true audiophile sound system, built by the team behind London's Brilliant Corners. Runs in the basement of a Vietnamese kitchen that stays open long after the DJs start.

name: ATOMECA Wine Bar
reason: Schofield's own second act on The Avenue. A walk-in wine list built around small plates, separate from the cocktail bar next door.

name: Hope Mill Theatre
reason: A converted cotton mill on Pollard Street, opened by two directors chasing Off West End intimacy. Fringe Venue of the Year, and every seat close enough to see the actors breathe.

name: Another Hand
reason: Twenty-four covers up a flight of painted steps on Deansgate Mews. Low-intervention plates built around whatever Cinderwood's growers sent over that morning.

name: King Street Townhouse Spa
reason: A subterranean ESPA spa under a Grade II Italianate former bank on King Street, Himalayan salt cave included. The infinity pool upstairs is for hotel residents only — the day spa isn't.

name: Evelyn's Cafe Bar
reason: Brunch classics by day, then the charcoal Inka grill takes over after dark. Persian and Pan-Asian small plates in a room that doesn't commit to one meal.

name: Waugh Brow Farm Shop
reason: Dave and Ruth Jones's own cattle and pigs, twenty yards from the counter that sells them. A working farm since 1985, with a café for people who came for bacon and stayed for cake.

name: Flawd Wine
reason: A waterside bottle shop on the New Islington marina that doubles as a bar. Walk-ins only, a cheese board built to match whatever's open, and a wine list that skips the conventional stuff.

name: Reserve at The Rex
reason: Three separate terraces above a former bank on King Street, each with its own name and its own best hour of the day. Get there before the swing band starts if you want a seat outside.

name: Riddles
reason: A 1920s room the size of a living room on Greenwood Street, yards from the market. Emma's own list of Prohibition-era cocktails, poured properly.

name: Speak In Code
reason: No sign on Jackson's Row, just a door. Inside: entirely plant-based small plates, and a cocktail list built on the bar's own fermentations, running to 2am.

name: Bar Shrimp
reason: Seafood snacks and cocktails under one mood-lit roof on New York Street. Built by the Higher Ground and Flawd team, and the sound system does as much work as the bar.

name: Manchester Rare Books
reason: A former waiting room on platform one, stocked with pre-loved and hard-to-find titles, plus a shelf of film and music ephemera.

name: Charlie Brown's Hale
reason: The former GupShup site on Ashley Road, made over into a corner gastro bar. Signature cocktails get equal billing with the food here, not an afterthought.

name: esea contemporary
reason: The UK's only art centre built around East and Southeast Asian practice, in an RIBA award-winning Market Buildings conversion on Thomas Street. Free to walk into.

name: Mobberley Cricket Club
reason: Founded 1876, still on Church Lane. A clubhouse bar and a viewing rail over a Cheshire outfield — much the same afternoon it's always been.

name: Bacchus
reason: A dedicated Champagne bar and a wine list built by the owners themselves, in a converted Village cottage. Mike Williams' kitchen behind it once ran Moss Nook.

name: The Legh Arms
reason: Twelve ensuite rooms above a 17th-century coaching inn on the Village green. Easy to turn a dinner booking into a reason to stay the night.

name: Delhi Dream
reason: Mahipal and Sunita's own kitchen on Turves Road. Proper Punjabi cooking that never bothered opening a second site.

name: LI~LY
reason: Aiden Byrne's tasting menu inside a 400-year-old timbered building on King Street. Three AA Rosettes and a Michelin Guide listing, in a room that seats a genuine handful.

name: Wallop
reason: A neighbourhood wine bar with two small siblings, in Didsbury and Prestwich. Live music some nights, and a King Street terrace that fills first.

name: Archive Bar & Bottle
reason: Two floors on Mellor Road. Real ale downstairs, a proper gin and cocktail list up top.

name: Thorn Grove Park
reason: Seven and a half acres in the middle of the village. Bowls green, open lawn, and quieter than the postcode suggests.

name: The Olde School
reason: A converted schoolroom on the Village green, open four days a week for wholesome plates and coffee. The wine list is bigger than you'd expect from a place this size.

name: Oil Art Advisory Gallery
reason: Zoe Garner's own two floors on King Street, opened 2024. Emerging names shown alongside the established.

name: Little Yang Sing
reason: A basement on the George Street corner, twenty-odd years into the same Cantonese repertoire. The dim sum trolley Chinatown's newer rooms still measure themselves against.

name: Hale Wine Bar
reason: Folding windows onto Ashley Road, and a wine list built by someone who left the big pub groups to run it their own way.

name: La Cucina
reason: Wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta on London Road, cocktails at the same counter. One of the few genuine independents on Alderley Edge's chain-heavy strip.

name: Dexter & Jones
reason: A thousand beers and three hundred gins behind the counter, but it's Adam and Katy Rickitt's own wine picks worth pulling up a stool for.

name: Contemporary Six Hale
reason: Alex Reuben's second room, on Ashley Road in the space Clark Art left behind. Contemporary names get the same quiet run of wall as the Manchester original.

name: Wong Wong Bakery
reason: Twenty-plus years on Princess Street, family-run, and the egg tarts are usually gone by mid-afternoon on a Saturday.

name: Rococo
reason: Taz and her daughter Faye's own shop on the high street. Soft furnishings, glassware, and one dressing-up rail of preloved designer pieces at the back.

name: The Foxhole
reason: Kip Evans' own boutique bar. Gins from round the world, four craft beers on tap, and a cheeseboard built to match whichever bottle you land on.

name: Lilac Cottage Tapas & Wine Bar
reason: Haseena and Felipe's own oak-beamed cottage on New Road. Tapas built for sharing, and a wine list with plenty to work through.

name: Chads Theatre
reason: A hundred-and-four-seat house run by the town's own amateur society since just after the First World War. Four main plays and two youth productions a year, coffee lounge included.

name: Bruntwood Park
reason: Formal gardens and a duck pond, a short walk from the station. Enough to build an actual Sunday around.

name: Inventery
reason: Ian Jones' own free-of-tie bar in a former retail unit on Station Road. Cocktails and small plates, with nothing on the price list dictated by a brewery.

name: Manchester Craft and Design Centre
reason: Eighteen working studio boutiques inside a converted Victorian fish and poultry market on Oak Street. Watch a maker at the bench, then buy the piece straight from them.

name: The Frog and Bucket
reason: Dave Perkin has run this from the same Oldham Street room since 1994 — new-material nights midweek, the big names still working out a new hour rather than touring the finished one.

name: The Whiskey Jar
reason: Two floors of a Grade I-listed mill on Tariff Street — Japanese and bourbon bottles upstairs, a proper sound system in the basement once the room's warmed up.

name: Port Street Beer House
reason: Seven handpumps of mostly Northern beer and a garden that empties the indoor room the moment the sun's out. No food menu — that was never really the point.

name: The Horsfall
reason: A three-storey Victorian shop on Great Ancoats Street, named for the philanthropist who opened the country's first art museum here in 1884. Free exhibitions and open studio sessions, run by the mental health charity that revived the building.

name: Bar Etna
reason: Sicilian, family-run, and unbothered by the market's queues two streets over. Fresh pasta and pistachio everything, from a kitchen that still runs its own deli counter.

name: Knutcraft at the Ruskin Rooms
reason: A Grade II-listed former reading room and fire station on Drury Lane, now a pottery-painting studio. Bring Your Own Bottle evenings for adults who'd rather glaze a plate than scroll past one.

name: Mobberley Ice Cream Coffee House
reason: A working dairy farm on Church Lane doing its own ice cream, its own coffee roast, and a proper afternoon tea. Order the sundae, then walk it off past the herd that made it.

name: Yuzu
reason: Twenty-five covers on Faulkner Street, no bookings for most sittings, BYOB. The ramen broth's been simmering since before Chinatown's newer rooms opened, and the queue since 2012 still hasn't thinned.

name: One Eight Six
reason: A barbershop by day on the old Deansgate courthouse corner. Find the mirrored door after dark and it's live soul and Motown until the small hours.

name: Arcane
reason: A basement two friends built off King Street, no sign worth mentioning above ground. Cocktails poured without the queue Deansgate's louder rooms carry.

name: KLUB
reason: A one-woman-built rooftop salon above Manchester Hall's old Freemasons' hall. One-to-one treatments, not a timetable to fit yourself around.

name: Portland Wine
reason: An Ashley Road institution that still runs its own tastings. A glass of fizz on arrival, five wines poured through, and a port to finish before you've decided what to take home.

name: Contemporary Six
reason: Alex Reuben's original room on Princess Street, by the Town Hall's side door. Forty-odd artists on rotation, an Own Art scheme that lets you pay monthly, and the space that later gave Hale its own quieter twin.

name: K2 Karaoke
reason: Thirty private booths across two George Street floors, right in the middle of Chinatown. The obvious answer if the night calls for your own soundtrack.

name: Pip
reason: Mary-Ellen McTague's return to the city she left Aumbry in, cooking low-waste, seasonal British plates on the ground floor of the Treehouse. A Michelin Guide listing within its first year.

name: Portfolio
reason: Julian Pizer and Cameron Foster's own cellar made public on Bridge Street. 250-odd Champagnes from more than seventy growers, a wall of a hundred bottles to read while you decide, and single-bite dishes built to match whichever one you land on.

name: HARCOURT
reason: Brian Hung and Priscilla So's Hong Kong-inspired free house on Stamford New Road. Fourteen taps of proper cask and craft, and small plates built from Hong Kong's own street food, not a brewery's set menu.

name: Butchers Bar
reason: Turtons' old shop on Ashley Road, empty three years, reborn as Ben Shepherd's own stage and skylight. Cocktails poured at the counter where the meat used to hang, and live sets most nights instead of a jukebox.

name: Neki
reason: Daniel Nechita's own room on King Street since 2019. Scratch-made brunch, paninis, and a house coffee blend nobody else in Knutsford pours.

name: Mobberley Village Bakers
reason: Thirty-four years trading under the Goostrey's name on Town Lane, and still the reason half the village has flour on its hands before nine.

name: Ancoats Coffee Co
reason: Roasting on site inside Royal Mills since 2013. The beans leave for cafés across the city every morning, but the counter seats here get first pour.

name: The Edge Theatre & Arts Centre
reason: A former Red Cross hospital on Manchester Road doing triple duty as Chorlton's theatre, gallery and community cinema. The programme turns over often enough that a second visit rarely repeats the first.

name: The Chorlton Tap
reason: Wilbraham Road's real-ale room since the late nineties, back when it was just called The Bar. Fourteen keg lines, four cask, and a wood-fired oven doing pizza out front some nights.

name: Bar San Juan
reason: Fifteen years on Beech Road and counting. Proper Spanish tapas, sherry by the glass, and a Neighbourhood Venue of the Year plaque behind the bar the locals would say is deserved.

name: White Peak Alpaca Farm
reason: Jake and Joanna's own herd on Paddock Hill, pre-booked walks only. A slow Cheshire afternoon that doesn't need a restaurant attached to justify the drive out.

name: Inch Arts
reason: The old town library's ground floor, now a working charity of studios, a makerspace, and a gallery that turns over as often as the artists teaching in it. Free to walk into, on Stamford New Road.

name: The Blind Pig
reason: A courtyard door off King Street with no sign worth mentioning. Four keg lines, a cocktail list that never quite repeats itself, and Porto next door if the wait's too long.

name: InHale Yoga
reason: A first-floor studio on Cecil Road running vinyasa before work and ashtanga after it. Small classes, real teachers' names on the timetable, not a franchise's booking app.

name: Lions Den
reason: Two hundred capacity on Deansgate Mews, built and still run by one promoter twenty years into the job. Open mic on a Wednesday, a proper touring act by the weekend.

name: Australasia
reason: A glass pyramid entrance on The Avenue, and a Pacific Rim share-plates menu re-set under new ownership last year. Sushi and southeast Asian flavours in the basement room that started Spinningfields' whole restaurant scene back in 2011.

name: Lime Tree
reason: Chef-patron Patrick Hannity's own room on Lapwing Lane since 1987. The menu turns over weekly, but the crispy duck stays by popular demand.

name: Volta
reason: The Unabombers' Burton Road room. Globally-inspired small plates, a Sunday roast worth planning round, and dog-friendly.

name: Saison
reason: David Bell's beer-first successor to the old Violet Hour on Burton Road. A serious keg and cask list, small plates built to match it, and cocktails for whoever didn't come for the beer.

name: Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden
reason: Ninety acres gifted to the city in 1915. The rockery and alpine beds still do their job, ten minutes from the village and a different pace entirely.

name: The Jane Eyre Chorlton
reason: Ancoats' cocktail room did well enough to earn a second, bigger kitchen on Beech Road. Same curated list, more room for families at Sunday roast.

name: Casa de Moor
reason: Mediterranean small plates and a cocktail list in the old Zitano room on Beech Road. Same ownership as Heaton Moor's Casa De Casa, though each kitchen runs its own name and its own menu now.

name: Henry's Cafe
reason: Natalie's own café in the old Post Office on The Village. Homemade cakes, a dog under every second table, and breakfast that's allowed to run into afternoon tea.

name: Knutsford Heritage Centre
reason: A reconstructed 17th-century forge on King Street, run entirely by volunteers. The Millennium Tapestry runs thirteen metres round two galleries, and admission is whatever you leave in the box.

name: Altrincham Little Theatre
reason: A hundred and thirty seats, and a drama society older than the building it's in. Amateur only in the sense that nobody's paid.

name: Festival Hall
reason: The parish's own 1927 assembly rooms, licensed bar included. Comedy nights and orchestral programmes share a stage built for a music festival that's still running, just under a different name now.

name: The Mucky Pup
reason: An Irish bar on Grove Street with live sets Friday through Sunday, and a pint of Guinness regulars swear tastes like it was poured in Dublin.
